evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We support monthly immunization camps in 48 villages in Udaipur district, Rajasthan. Each village's camp runs on a fixed day each month, 9am to 2pm, at the anganwadi center. Our register holds every enrolled child's next due dose and the camp date. In exit interviews at 12 camps and a survey of 600 mothers, 64% of mothers whose child missed a dose said they did not know the camp was that day or that week; vaccine stock has been reliable for two years, the vaccines are free, and nobody mentioned distrust. About 60% of households have a phone, usually held by the husband; many mothers cannot read a Hindi text; the ASHA visits each hamlet weekly; our call center can place voice calls in Mewari. Design the reminder schedule.
evals.expected_output: A reminder schedule in the output template that uses voice calls and the ASHA rather than Hindi text messages, with a ceiling and a stop rule for every send.
assertions: Every send in the table has a channel, what the message must name, and a condition that stops it.
Chooses a voice call or a visit over a Hindi text, citing who holds the phone or who can read.
States the most contacts per month and how a household opts out.
Says who the calls do not reach and what those households get instead.
Gives the levels of opt-out or response at which the schedule is reviewed.
Promises no effect size for this program.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Patients keep missing their follow-up appointments. Set up SMS reminders.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the evidence that forgetting is the barrier, how the program knows each patient's date, and who holds the phone, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks what shows that patients intend to come and forget, rather than being stopped by cost, distance, or distrust.
Asks how appointments are dated and how the program knows each patient's date.
Asks who holds the phone, whether it is shared, or whether the patient reads.
Does not produce a reminder schedule.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Patients at our HIV treatment clinic in Kisumu, Kenya miss doses. In interviews most say they simply forget on busy days; drugs are free and in stock. We want to send a daily SMS at 8pm saying 'Take your two tablets now'. The clinic's register has every patient's phone number and refill date. Some patients share a phone with family. Design the schedule.
evals.expected_output: The skill designs a schedule of no more than one message a week that names no drug, dose, or condition, and says a clinician or pharmacist and a privacy lead must review it before the first send.
assertions: Sets a ceiling of no more than one message a week rather than the daily message requested.
The message content does not name tablets, a dose, HIV, or the clinic's purpose.
Names a clinician or pharmacist to approve what a message about medication names.
Names a privacy or safeguarding review because some patients share a phone.
Says what to bring to those specialists.
Does not present the schedule as ready to send without those reviews.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: At the camp we want each mother to tell the ASHA when and where she will bring the child for the next dose, and write it on the immunization card. Can you design that?
evals.expected_output: The skill says this is a plan the mother makes, not a message the program sends, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says a plan the person states is different from a reminder the program sends.
Does not produce a reminder schedule.
